title: Basic starter questions.
author: myvarequals
selftext:
I just started using my left over usage on my Chat Plus sub to create a simple pixel art top down shooter with Godot and Codex. Some free gfx/sprite assets from a website.

What level model are most people using for general tasks? I know the higher models are better for architecture and lower models for the trivial grunt work stuff, but is it even worth dabbling with Astra?

I was using Astra High to get the first scene set up and characters, but it felt like it was eating through my usage. It also liked to test a lot which would sometimes consume more than it did to make changes to the codebase. Do most of you do your own testing? Or use a lower model for the testing? 

Just looking for some general guidance and thoughts on what other users are doing.

Thanks for reading!

comments.author: JJBareaIsLeFather
comments.body: I don't know, I only use Opus 5.5 and Astra 6 right now, the rest is childs play

comments.author: ExampleCute6496
comments.body: You should use Codex with GPT 6.1 Sol with GPT-6-Luna as a subagent for dumb tasks like research. Sol is a bit weird and literal in instruction following, but it will deliver solid code quality. Maybe use Astra only for high-level direction and planning, and always switch to Sol for implementation unless you're doing something very very complex.

replies.author: myvarequals
replies.body: This was the mentality I was leaning toward, wasn’t sure if I should use the 5 or 6 models.

comments.author: Sozobi
comments.body:
I would definitely not be using Astra for any actual coding work, your usage will be gone in 5 minutes. I mainly use Astra as a brainstormer or to discuss various ideas and plans for the game, create in-game screenshots and reference material to find the game look you are going for, and then those documents can be used by the AI who will actually make the game.

As many others, I use Opus 5.5 (medium) with Claude Code and it's truly amazing. It gets so much work done within your usage limits. I am building a 1st person zombie survivor with it from scratch and in about 2 weeks, I've gone from just an idea to almost a fully playable demo with animations, zombie spawn system, procedurally generated houses, items and weapons, lockpick system, interactive map. I have Opus 5.5 working in Blender as well, making all the models, rigs, animations and textures, it makes all the sounds automatically via ElevenLabs and hooks them into the game.

If you move to Opus 5.5, try and set it up like a little developement studio, splitting the work out among sub-agents. I have an agent for Blender, an agent for Unity, and an agent for sound work and they can all work at the same time. You have to imagine yourself as the creative lead/art director with the overall idea, and then imagine you are recruiting members for your dev team, telling them what their roles and skills are, etc.

replies.author: myvarequals
replies.body: This sounds solid, I’m gonna try the agents.

comments.author: Randy-Chileno
comments.body: What i do is use Claude free, to make a motor, then chat gpt plus for cats majority, then codex for more complex tasks, Astra for specific errors But mostly for debug.

comments.author: BHTAelitepwn
comments.body: Sol 6.1 does a more than decent job. Astra for only the most difficult / important tasks.

replies.author: myvarequals
replies.body: I did switch to this briefly before posting and the usage was about half or less than what I was doing with Astra. Thanks for the reply.
